newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Quinn examining extension of car scrappage scheme.
newsitem.headline: Quinn examining extension of car scrappage scheme.

text.p: Irish finance minister Ruairi Quinn said on Thursday that he was considering the extension of a car scrappage scheme which expires at the end of the year.
The scheme, which was introduced in July 1995, allowed vehicle registration tax relief of 1,000 punts where a new car was purchased and an old car was scrapped.

Quinn told the annual conference of the Society of the Irish Motor Industry (SIMI) that its request for an extension for a further year was being examined "with particular reference to its impact on safety, the environment and, of course, Exchequer returns".
Quinn also announced that the government had decided to abolish the special advance value-added-tax (VAT) payment made in December each year by the largest VAT remitters.
Payment is currently made by firms with an annual net VAT liability of one million punts or more.

Abolition of the payment will give rise to a once-off cashflow cost to the Exchequer of around 120 million punts in 1996 but will not affect the budgetary position in 1997 or in subsequent years, Quinn said.
